title: A taxonomy of epistemic injustice in the context of AI and the case for generative hermeneutical erasure

bias_targets.methodology: Philosophical and conceptual analysis synthesizing literature to form a taxonomy of epistemic injustice, focusing on 'epistemic colonization' and 'generative hermeneutical erasure' via the overrepresentation of WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, Democratic) perspectives and the suppression of non-Western epistemologies (e.g., Akan ontology).

Theoretical evaluation using literature case studies to illustrate 'generative hermeneutical access' issues, such as unequal model performance, mistranslations, and skewed narrative representations in under-resourced and non-English languages.

Conceptual analysis of 'amplified testimonial injustice' using hypothetical and real-world scenarios (e.g., chatbots reproducing stereotypes about immigrants or generating racially biased imagery) to evaluate how generative AI structurally amplifies existing societal prejudices.
